name: GSG probe on a short, bad contact

example.note: The same short with a 0.5 Ω contact. The TDR after the short sits at 0.5 Ω, more than a decade above a good landing, and |S11| reads about −0.17 dB instead of 0 dB. A bad signal tip and two bad ground tips look alike: both put resistance in the one current loop, so a one-port can’t tell which. One lifted ground mostly adds inductance (the grounds were in parallel); raise the L chip and the edge barely moves. Set R to 1 MΩ for a probe that never landed.
example.author: TDR Painter
